text:
maya: quick design question — the new priority rail gets really long when a policy has 10+ rules, feels hard to scan. open to swapping to a condensed 'dense' mode? :thinking:

samir: agree. main problem is the visual weight of each card. if we reduce padding and flatten the shadow it's way easier to scan. also the drag handle currently overlaps focus styles.

olivia: +1 to dense mode toggle. downside: might hide some rule metadata that people rely on. could we collapse descriptions by default and show icons for key attrs (region, model, override)?

maya: exactly — icons would help. also thinking about keyboard reorder: right now arrow-reorder requires focus on the handle which is tiny. propose a persistent "reorder mode" button that locks the list and exposes larger targets and up/down buttons.

jess: accessibility nit: when reordering via keyboard we need aria-live to announce "Rule X moved to position Y". current preview doesn't announce any moves so screenreader users lose context.

samir: good call. also saw a validation edge case in the simulator: when two rules have identical priority and conflicting actions, the preview shows both paths but there's no inline validation message — only a toast after run. we should surface a tight inline validation badge on the conflicting rules themselves.

olivia: agree — inline is better. propose a small warning pill under the rule title: "priority clash" with a tooltip explaining fallback behavior and suggested fix (e.g., bump priority or add a guard).

maya: mock idea: add a tiny heatmap strip in the preview timeline showing rule coverage frequency across simulated traffic. helps confirm which rules are actually selected most. small, low-contrast so it doesn't dominate.

deploy-bot: preview-sim: updated with heatmap strip (staging). run `preview-sim --policy 42 --sample 1000` to refresh.

jess: UX question — does heatmap need legend? maybe hover shows counts. for color choices please keep >=3:1 contrast for low-vision users.

maya: hover counts + legend in the panel footer works. also let's add a compact tooltip copy for the warning pill: one sentence, action-forward (e.g., "Two rules share priority; add a guard or change priority to ensure deterministic routing.").

samir: next steps: olivia to iterate mock with dense toggle + icons, jess to write aria announcements for reorder and preview heatmap, maya to spec inline validation copy. i'll put a short doc in Figma comments and tag you all. :thumbsup:

olivia: on it — aiming for mock update by EOD Friday.

maya: thanks!
